summary: Cameras, lenses, lighting, drones, and photography accessories. Trend data (May 2026): 'sell used camera equipment' is a top query (interest 100), 'used photography equipment' at 81 — the resale demand is structural. KEH, MPB, Adorama are the major used-photo retailers (their pricing sets the market floor). Camera body resale is heavily generation-dependent (a Canon R5 holds value; a 5D Mark II is a thrift-tier item). Lenses age more gracefully — a 1990s Canon 70-200 f/2.8L still sells well. Vintage film cameras have a dedicated collector ecosystem (Contax, Leica M, Mamiya). Drones (DJI specifically) hold value remarkably well due to FAA-registration friction.
field_workflow: ALWAYS verify shutter count for DSLRs (camera body life is rated 100k-400k actuations)
Lenses: check for fungus (lens-fungus is a deal-killer), separation, scratches on front element
Sensor cleanliness: check with sensor-loupe photo against blank wall
Original box / cables / charger / battery / strap = +20-30%
Mounting standard matters: Canon EF ≠ Canon RF, Sony E ≠ Sony A-mount
Test all features: AF, IBIS, EVF, manual focus rings smooth, aperture blades clean
Lens elements: front + rear + internal — use a flashlight to spot dust/fungus
DJI: registered to seller's account = friction; confirm unbinding before purchase

era_markers: Canon EOS branding with model number
RF mount (mirrorless 2018+) vs EF mount (DSLR legacy)
L-series red ring on lens = pro tier
USM (Ultrasonic Motor) vs STM (Stepping Motor) — USM premium
Made in Japan stamping (older premium)
Original box, charger, battery, strap, manual = +20-30%
Shutter count <50k = like-new

comp_ranges_usd.item: EOS R5 Mark II / R5 body
EOS R6 Mark II / R6 body

brands.notes: L-series lenses (red ring) are the resale champions — they hold value across decades. Bodies depreciate faster than lenses. R-mount RF lenses (mirrorless) are current-gen; EF lenses (DSLR) still sell strongly because Canon ships an EF→RF adapter. The 70-200 f/2.8L is an icon — sells consistently across all generations.

era_markers: Nikon branding + Z mount (mirrorless 2018+) or F mount (DSLR)
S-series Z lenses = pro tier (premium over standard Z)
Gold ring on F-mount Nikkor lenses = pro tier
VR (Vibration Reduction) marker premium
Made in Japan stamping
Original box, charger, battery, strap, manual = +20-30%
Shutter count <50k for D-series (D850 rated ~200k)
brands.notes: Nikon's transition to Z-mount has been slower than Canon's RF transition — the F-mount lens ecosystem still has massive aftermarket value. AF-S Nikkor pro-glass (gold ring) is a perpetual seller. Z lenses are smaller market but premium tier.

era_markers: Sony Alpha (a-prefix) cameras
Sony FE = full-frame mirrorless lens line
Sony E = APS-C crop lens line
G Master (GM) = pro-tier lenses (orange G logo on lens)
Original Sony retail packaging + battery + strap + body cap
brands.notes: Sony's E-mount system is currently the most-active mirrorless ecosystem. a7-series is the workhorse line; a1 is the tournament-tier flagship. G Master lenses are the resale standouts (each sells for $1,500-$2,500 used).

era_markers: Fujifilm / Fuji branding with X-series or GFX line
X-Trans CMOS sensor = APS-C series (X-T, X-Pro, X100, X-H)
GFX = medium format digital
Original Fuji packaging (bright orange + black)
X100V / X100VI fixed-lens compact (cult favorite)
brands.notes: X100V / X100VI (fixed-lens compact) is a cult favorite — discontinued + waitlisted models trade at retail-plus pricing. GFX medium format is the secondary-market alternative to Hasselblad. X-Trans sensor + Fuji film simulations are the core appeal.

era_markers: Leica red dot logo (essential for authentication)
Made in Germany / Wetzlar stamping
M-mount rangefinder = bayonet mount
Lens designation: Summicron (f/2), Summilux (f/1.4), Elmarit (f/2.8), Noctilux (f/0.95-1.0)
Original Leica box + leather pouch + cap = +30-40%
Black paint vs chrome (collector premium for black paint)
brands.notes: Leica is the photography blue-chip brand — values appreciate over time, especially for film M-bodies and discontinued lenses. Counterfeits exist for older models (M3 / M4 era); verify serial number against Leica's records. Always inspect rangefinder calibration on M-bodies.

era_markers: Hasselblad branding (Sweden) with model series
V-System = 6x6 medium format film (500-series)
H-System = digital + film medium format
X-System = mirrorless medium format (current digital)
Carl Zeiss lenses on V-system (red T* coating premium)
Hasselblad-marked / Phase One backs
brands.notes: V-system 500-series film cameras have a sustained collector + working-photographer market. X-system (mirrorless medium format) is the current digital line. Always verify dark-slide function on V-system bodies.

era_markers: Sigma branding with Art / Sport / Contemporary line
DG DN designation = mirrorless full-frame native
Mount tag (Sony E / Canon RF / Nikon Z / L-mount / Canon EF / Nikon F)
Hyper Sonic Motor (HSM) marker
Original lens hood + pouch + caps = +10-15%
brands.notes: Sigma Art lenses are the consensus best-third-party glass. Mount-specific (Sony E version sells differently from Canon RF). 18-35 f/1.8 is the unique APS-C zoom that has no first-party equivalent — sustained demand.

era_markers: Tamron branding
G2 designation = generation 2 (premium over original)
SP = Superior Performance line (older legacy)
Mount-specific (Sony E / Canon EF / Nikon F)
brands.notes: Tamron 28-75 f/2.8 is the famous lightweight Sony-E alternative to the Sony FE 24-70 GM at half the price. The 35-150 f/2-2.8 is a unique focal range — no first-party equivalent. Strong third-party glass.

era_markers: Zeiss branding (Carl Zeiss for older / Zeiss for current)
Otus = manual focus flagship
Milvus = manual focus DSLR (Canon EF / Nikon F)
Loxia = manual focus Sony E full-frame
Batis = autofocus Sony E full-frame
T* coating marker (red star)
brands.notes: Zeiss is the premium third-party glass tier. Otus is uncompromising flagship MF; Milvus is Otus-derived DSLR; Loxia/Batis are Sony E mirrorless. Smaller market than Sigma but rabid collector following.

era_markers: Olympus / OM SYSTEM branding (renamed 2022)
PRO designation on M.Zuiko lenses = pro tier
OM-D = Micro Four Thirds digital
OM = vintage 35mm SLR (1972-2003 cult collectible)
Made in Japan stamping
brands.notes: Micro Four Thirds (M4/3) has a smaller sensor footprint but compact-system advantage — OM SYSTEM is the dominant brand. Vintage OM-system 35mm SLRs (1970s-90s) have a strong collector base; OM-2n + 50mm f/1.4 Zuiko is the iconic combo.

era_markers: Panasonic Lumix branding
S = full-frame L-mount (S1/S5/S9 series)
G = Micro Four Thirds (GH/G9/G100 series)
Leica DG co-branded lenses (premium tier)
GH-series = pro video flagship line
brands.notes: Panasonic GH-series is the de-facto indie cinema camera — videographers buy them used aggressively. S-series is Panasonic's L-mount full-frame entry (sister system with Leica SL + Sigma fp). Strong video credentials drive the resale.

era_markers: DJI branding with model line (Mavic / Mini / Phantom / Inspire / Avata / Ronin / Osmo)
Original retail packaging with serial number
Charging hub / Fly More combo accessories
Battery cycle count (each battery has hours-of-flight history)
Activated to seller's account vs unbound (unbound = ready for new owner)
brands.notes: DJI dominates consumer drones. CRITICAL: drones must be unbound from seller's DJI account before transfer — sellers sometimes forget and the new owner has friction. FAA-registration is buyer's responsibility (>0.55lb drones need it). Original Fly More combos add 30-50% to standalone drone resale.

era_markers: Profoto branding (Sweden) for premium
Godox branding for value tier
Battery vs AC strobes (location vs studio)
Original modifier mount (Profoto / Bowens / Godox AC)
brands.notes: Profoto is the studio-strobe premium tier. Godox is the value-tier challenger that's taken massive market share. Used Profoto sells at 50-70% of new MSRP for years; Godox depreciates slightly faster but used demand is huge.

platform_notes.eBay: Dominant marketplace for used camera equipment.
platform_notes.KEH: Largest used-camera retailer in the US — wholesale buyer too. Their offer prices are the floor; eBay used clears at 110-130% of KEH's offer.
platform_notes.MPB: European-headquartered used-camera retailer with strong US presence — similar economics to KEH.
platform_notes.Adorama Used: Retailer used-trade-in section — sets a price ceiling; eBay used always sells below Adorama Used asking.
platform_notes.B&H Used: Smaller used inventory than KEH/MPB but their prices set the high-end of the market for premium glass.
